new.title: Discover the Carthusians at the Musée de la Grande Chartreuse
new.desc: The museum occupies La Correrie, the former working quarters of the Carthusian lay brothers, and is the only part of the Grande Chartreuse complex open to visitors. Founded in 1957, it tells about 900 years of the Carthusian order through documents, films, a Renaissance room with a model of the monastery and a collection of Chartreuse maps.
new.tip: Visits are by reservation, so book through the museum website. The T40 bus from Grenoble stops at La Correrie, then it is a 15-minute walk uphill.
new.q: Musée de la Grande Chartreuse, La Correrie, Saint-Pierre-de-Chartreuse

new.title: Tour the Caves de la Chartreuse and taste the liqueurs in Voiron
new.desc: The Caves de la Chartreuse in Voiron are the former distillery cellars of the famous green and yellow liqueur made by the Carthusian monks. The guided visit ends with a tasting of the green and yellow Chartreuse or an alcohol-free herbal tea, and the shop sells the full range.
new.tip: Visits are guided and should be booked on chartreuse.fr. The shop at 10 boulevard Edgar Kofler is open daily.
new.q: Caves de la Chartreuse, 10 boulevard Edgar Kofler, Voiron

new.title: Admire the hanging houses of Pont-en-Royans
new.desc: Colourful 16th-century houses cling to the cliff and overhang the Bourne river at the entrance to the Gorges de la Bourne. The village has been a protected site since 1944 and inspired Stendhal.
new.tip: The best views are from the left bank of the Bourne or from the Pont Picard; follow the signs marked Maisons suspendues.
new.q: Maisons suspendues, Pont-en-Royans

new.title: Walk under the soda-straw stalactites of the Grottes de Choranche
new.desc: This show cave in the Vercors is famous for its fistulous stalactites, hollow soda straws that hang from the ceiling in great numbers. Visits are guided and include a lit route with a sound-and-light show, and the site has a panoramic terrace and bar.
new.tip: Guided visit only, with online booking on visites-nature-vercors.com. Parking is free; allow about 1h45 on site.
new.q: Grottes de Choranche, route des grottes, Choranche

new.title: Ride the Pic Blanc cable car above Alpe d'Huez
new.desc: The Pic Blanc cable car, opened in the early 1960s, carries visitors from Alpe d'Huez to the 3,330 m summit above the Sarenne glacier. It is a summer sightseeing and hiking lift as well as the gateway to the glacier skiing of the resort.
new.tip: Summer operation is listed for July and August at about 23 EUR per day; check the resort site for current dates and prices.
new.q: Téléphérique du Pic Blanc, Alpe d'Huez

new.title: See the Roman Temple of Augustus and Livia in Vienne
new.desc: Built for the imperial cult around the turn of the era, this hexastyle Corinthian temple on a raised podium measures about 24 by 14 metres. It is one of only two such temples in France, alongside the Maison Carrée in Nîmes, and later served as a church, a Temple of Reason and a museum.
new.tip: The exterior can be seen at any time from Place du Palais. Combine it with the nearby theatre and cathedral on a Vienne walk.
new.q: Temple d'Auguste et de Livie, Place du Palais, Vienne

new.title: Sit in the Roman theatre of Vienne on the hillside
new.desc: Dating from about 40 to 50 AD, the Théâtre Antique is one of the largest Roman urban theatres in Gaul and seats about 7,500. Since 1981 it has been the main stage of the Jazz à Vienne festival.
new.tip: Visit during the day to climb the tiers; during the festival, ticketed concerts take over the site.
new.q: Théâtre Antique, Rue du Cirque, Vienne

new.title: Step inside Saint-Maurice, the old cathedral of Vienne
new.desc: Construction of this Romanesque and Gothic church began in the 11th to 12th century and was completed in the 16th. It was consecrated in 1251, sacked by Huguenots in 1562 and classified as a historic monument in 1840. Its facing is fragile molasse stone, restored in 2021 to 2022.
new.tip: It stands on Place Saint-Maurice in the old town; look at the carved west front and the Romanesque nave.
new.q: Cathédrale Saint-Maurice, Place Saint-Maurice, Vienne

new.title: Wander the medieval streets and covered market of Crémieu
new.desc: Crémieu is a fortified medieval town in the Balcons du Dauphiné with 14th-century gates such as the Porte de Lyon. Its timber market hall dates from 1433 to 1434 and has been a historic monument since 1906.
new.tip: The tourist office publishes a walking plan of the medieval city; the halle is the natural starting point.
new.q: Halles de Crémieu, Place de la Nation, Crémieu

new.title: Marvel at the Palais Idéal of Facteur Cheval in Hauterives
new.desc: Postman Ferdinand Cheval built this folk-art palace stone by stone in his garden over about 33 years, from 1879 to 1912. Its architecture borrows from mosque, Swiss chalet and Hindu temple, and he also built his own tomb in the Hauterives cemetery.
new.tip: Open daily with seasonal hours; allow about 1.5 hours and visit the tomb in the village cemetery too.
new.q: Palais Idéal du Facteur Cheval, 8 rue du Palais, Hauterives

new.title: Study the carved faces of the Maison des Têtes in Valence
new.desc: This Renaissance townhouse at 57 Grande Rue was built from 1528 to 1532 for law professor Antoine de Dorne. Its facade and square courtyard are covered with sculpted heads, and a young Bonaparte once lived in the town while at the artillery school.
new.tip: The courtyard is free to enter all year. It sits near Place des Clercs in the old centre.
new.q: Maison des Têtes, 57 Grande Rue, Valence

new.title: Taste your way through the Cité du Chocolat Valrhona
new.desc: Inaugurated in 2013 next to Valrhona's historic factory in Tain-l'Hermitage, this discovery centre has an interactive trail on cocoa and chocolate, workshops and a boutique. It reports more than one million visitors since opening.
new.tip: Open daily except 1 January, 1 May and 25 December. The Tain-Tournon station is a 10-minute walk away.
new.q: Cité du Chocolat Valrhona, 12 avenue du Président Roosevelt, Tain-l'Hermitage

new.title: Visit the Renaissance Château de Grignan of Madame de Sévigné
new.desc: The château overlooks the village where Madame de Sévigné stayed with her daughter, the comtesse de Grignan, and wrote many of her letters. A new visitor route opened in 2026, the 400th anniversary of her birth, with ten new rooms on the Grignan couple and the marquise.
new.tip: The marquise is buried in the collegiate church of Saint-Sauveur in the village. The château is closed on Tuesdays from November to March.
new.q: Château de Grignan, Montée du Château, Grignan

new.title: Climb the 52 m Tour de Crest for the Drôme valley view
new.desc: The keep of Crest dates from the 12th century and is described as the highest medieval keep in France at about 52 metres. It served as a state prison from the 15th to the 19th century and is a historic monument.
new.tip: The climb is about 524 steps; bring water and allow around an hour with the exhibition.
new.q: Tour de Crest, Montée de la Tour, Crest

new.title: Walk the ramparts of Briançon's Cité Vauban
new.desc: Briançon's walled upper town, rebuilt in the 17th and 18th centuries by Vauban's engineers, sits at 1,326 m and is among the highest towns in France. Its tiered defences were inscribed with the Fortifications of Vauban on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2008.
new.tip: The tourist office is in the Maison des Templiers; the Fort du Château can be visited on foot from late April to November.
new.q: Cité Vauban, Briançon

new.title: Cross the Pont d'Asfeld high above the Durance gorge
new.desc: This single-arch stone bridge was started around 1720 under the marquis d'Asfeld, following Vauban's 1700 idea, to link the upper town with the forts on the Trois Têtes plateau. It spans a gorge some 55 to 64 m deep and is part of the UNESCO Vauban listing.
new.tip: Free and open at all times; it is also a well-known spot for bungee jumping.
new.q: Pont d'Asfeld, Briançon

new.title: Admire Notre-Dame du Réal, the old cathedral of Embrun
new.desc: Built from about 1170 to 1225, at the transition from Romanesque to Gothic, it is described as the most important monument in the French Alps. Its Lombard-style bell tower influenced others, and the church was named after the kings who came to worship there, starting with Louis XI.
new.tip: Visit with the free visit guide from the town website and look for the Lombard porch.
new.q: Cathédrale Notre-Dame du Réal, Rue de l'Archevêché, Embrun

new.title: Explore the Vauban fortress town of Mont-Dauphin
new.desc: Vauban founded Mont-Dauphin in 1693 on the Guil-Durance confluence after a Piedmontese raid, and it is one of the 12 Vauban sites inscribed by UNESCO in 2008. It is a fortified town with civilian housing inside the walls, entered by the Porte de Briançon with its drawbridge.
new.tip: It lies on the RN94 about 36 km south of Briançon; guided and self-guided visits are available.
new.q: Place forte de Mont-Dauphin, Mont-Dauphin

new.title: Visit Fort Queyras on its rocky spur above the Guil
new.desc: A medieval castle reworked by Vauban from about 1700 stands on a rock spur above Château-Ville-Vieille, controlling the Guil valley. It is open in the warm months and visits take under an hour.
new.tip: Check fortqueyras.fr for dates; one listing gives 13 June to 20 September with the last entry at 17:00.
new.q: Fort Queyras, Château-Ville-Vieille

new.title: Stroll Saint-Véran, among Europe's highest villages, and its sundials
new.desc: Saint-Véran in the Queyras lies at about 2,040 m and is presented as the highest inhabited commune in Europe. Its houses carry more than two dozen painted sundials, the oldest dated 1840 on the church square, many by Zarbula.
new.tip: The village has a clear sky and an observatory; walk the lanes in the morning light to photograph the sundials.
new.q: Saint-Véran, Queyras

new.title: Ride the Glaciers de la Meije cable cars in La Grave
new.desc: Two cable-car sections have taken visitors since 1978 to the Col des Ruillans at 3,200 m, between the Meije (3,983 m) and the Girose glacier. The upper station has an ice grotto and a restaurant, and in winter the area is a famous freeride domain.
new.tip: The 2026 summer season ran from 6 June to 13 September; adult fares were around 40 EUR.
new.q: Téléphériques des Glaciers de la Meije, La Grave

new.title: Find the Romanesque Abbaye de Boscodon in its forest
new.desc: Monks of the Chalais order began this abbey in 1142 in the Boscodon forest near Embrun and Serre-Ponçon lake. It has been restored since 1972 by a friends' association and the abbey church and the abbot's chapel can be entered free.
new.tip: Opening times vary, so check the abbey's website or call 04 92 43 14 45 before going.
new.q: Abbaye de Boscodon, Crots

new.title: See the Chapelle Saint-Michel on its island in Serre-Ponçon
new.desc: This 12th-century chapel, destroyed in 1692 and rebuilt in the 17th century, escaped demolition when the dam was built. Its former hilltop is now a small island in the lake.
new.tip: Landing on the island is prohibited, so view it from the shore at the Baie Saint-Michel, east of the Savines bridge.
new.q: Chapelle Saint-Michel, Baie Saint-Michel, Prunières

new.title: Visit the abbey church of Saint-Antoine-l'Abbaye
new.desc: Works on this great abbey church began around 1130 and it was classified in 1840 by Prosper Mérimée. The village, once the seat of the Antonine order, is one of the Plus Beaux Villages de France and has a museum, Chroniques d'une abbaye.
new.tip: The village is about halfway between Valence and Grenoble; the museum is run by the Isère department.
new.q: Abbaye de Saint-Antoine-l'Abbaye, Saint-Antoine-l'Abbaye

new.title: Climb to the Château des Adhémar in Montélimar
new.desc: This medieval castle above Montélimar was enlarged into a palace by the Adhémar family in the 12th century and later served as a prison. Owned by the Drôme department, it forms a trio with the castles of Grignan and Suze-la-Rousse and has hosted a music festival since 2022.
new.tip: Check the Drôme tourism site for current opening hours before visiting.
new.q: Château des Adhémar, Montée du Château, Montélimar

new.title: Learn about the Noix de Grenoble at Le Grand Séchoir
new.desc: This museum in Vinay, opened in 2005, occupies an old farm with a restored walnut dryer and tells the story of the Grenoble walnut country. The shop sells walnut oil, cakes, nougat and other products.
new.tip: Opening days vary through the year; check the museum site. Regional bus T62 stops at Coopérative Noix.
new.q: Le Grand Séchoir, 705 route de Grenoble, Vinay

new.title: Discover the lake villages at the Musée archéologique du lac de Paladru
new.desc: The museum on the lakeshore at Charavines presents two excavated sites: the Neolithic village of Les Baigneurs and the fortified settlement of Colletière, from around the year 1000. The building is shaped like a dugout canoe.
new.tip: Reported opening Tuesday to Sunday with a lunch break; confirm times on the official site.
new.q: Musée archéologique du lac de Paladru, 51 rue du Musée, Charavines

new.title: Taste Montélimar nougat at the Arnaud Soubeyran Musée du Nougat
new.desc: Founded in 1837, the Arnaud Soubeyran house is described as the oldest of the nougatiers still making Montélimar nougat with the traditional recipe, cooked in copper cauldrons. Its factory and Musée du Nougat are at 22 avenue de Gournier, and Montélimar nougat obtained its IGP in 2024.
new.tip: Adult admission is around 5 EUR; the site is closed on 1 January and 25 December.
new.q: Fabrique Arnaud Soubeyran Musée du Nougat, 22 avenue de Gournier, Montélimar

new.title: Taste Clairette de Die at the Cave Jaillance
new.desc: The Cave de Die Jaillance stands at the entrance to Die when arriving from Valence, with an exhibition on the sparkling wine, the terroir and local legend. The visit is followed by a tasting of Clairette and Crémant de Die.
new.tip: Open year-round with guided visits; call 04 75 22 30 15 or check jaillance.com for times.
new.q: La Cave de Die Jaillance, avenue de Die, Die

new.title: Buy Nyons olive oil at the Moulin Dozol-Autrand
new.desc: This family mill at the foot of the Pont Roman dates from 1750 and has been run by fourteen generations of millers. It sells AOP Huile d'olive de Nyons and AOP Olives noires de Nyons, made from Tanche olives harvested in December.
new.tip: Try the tapenade and the black olives; the shop is by the Roman bridge.
new.q: Moulin Dozol-Autrand, Promenade de la Digue, Nyons

new.title: Taste Hermitage syrah on a Cave de Tain cellar visit
new.desc: The Cave de Tain at 22 route de Larnage offers guided visits with a tasting of five wines, four parcel selections and one Hermitage. Visits are run through the Terres de Syrah tourism arm.
new.tip: The tour costs about 16 EUR per adult; in spring and autumn it ran Saturday at 15:30 and Sunday at 10:30, so confirm before you go.
new.q: Cave de Tain, 22 route de Larnage, Tain-l'Hermitage

new.title: Try the pogne and the Suisse at Laurent Serre in Valence
new.desc: This boulanger-pâtissier in Grande Rue is praised by Gault&Millau for its pogne and its Suisse on orange shortcrust pastry. The Suisse is said to have been created in Valence in honour of the guards of Pope Pius VI, who died there in 1799.
new.tip: Ask for a pogne, the orange-blossom brioche, and a Suisse biscuit to take away.
new.q: Laurent Serre boulanger pâtissier, Grande Rue, Valence

new.title: Buy Saint-Marcellin IGP at the Étoile du Vercors dairy
new.desc: The cheese factory in Saint-Just-de-Claix makes and matures two Dauphiné cheeses, the Saint-Marcellin IGP and the Saint-Félicien, and has a shop open to the public. The Saint-Marcellin obtained its IGP in 2013.
new.tip: The shop is open Monday to Friday during the day (listing: Mon to Thu 8 to 12 and 13 to 17, Friday to 17:00).
new.q: Fromagerie de l'Étoile du Vercors, Saint-Just-de-Claix

new.title: Buy farmhouse Bleu du Vercors-Sassenage at Les Champs Derrière
new.desc: This family dairy farm in Villard-de-Lans sells farmhouse cheese including Bleu du Vercors-Sassenage, a raw cow's-milk blue with AOP status since 2001. The semi-soft cheese is sweet and creamy.
new.tip: Shop hours listed from September to December are 16:00 to 18:00 on most days and 10:00 to 12:00 plus 16:00 to 18:00 on Saturdays.
new.q: Fromagerie Les Champs Derrière, 846 route de la Côte 2000, Villard-de-Lans

new.title: Eat tourtons and Mont d'Or at Chez Natchou in Briançon
new.desc: A short walk from the Cité Vauban on Rue Général Rostolland, this restaurant serves home-style French food with Italian touches. Its mountain specialities include tourtons and hot Mont d'Or.
new.tip: Reserve in the ski and summer high seasons.
new.q: Chez Natchou, rue Général Rostolland, Briançon

new.title: Dine at the three-star Maison Pic in Valence
new.desc: Anne-Sophie Pic runs the family restaurant at 285 avenue Victor-Hugo, which holds three Michelin stars. The house first earned its stars under André Pic in 1939, and she regained the third in 2007.
new.tip: Closed Mondays and Sunday evenings; menus ran around 310 to 410 EUR in 2024, and Bistro André is the lighter option.
new.q: Maison Pic, 285 avenue Victor Hugo, Valence

new.title: Dine at La Pyramide, Fernand Point's legendary table in Vienne
new.desc: Once a three-star institution under Fernand Point, La Pyramide reopened in 1989 under Patrick and Pascale Henriroux, who regained two Michelin stars. It has been a Relais & Châteaux member since 1999.
new.tip: The 2026 to 2027 season lists à la carte at 52 to 115 EUR and the Menu Pyramide at 210 EUR; book ahead.
new.q: La Pyramide Patrick Henriroux, boulevard Fernand Point, Vienne

new.title: Eat tourtons du Champsaur at Papi Ours in Gap
new.desc: Papi Ours at 16 rue Pérolière is a specialist of the tourtons of the Hautes-Alpes, fried pastry pockets with savoury or sweet fillings. It is listed as open daily in 2026.
new.tip: Try a savoury tourton with salad then a sweet one with jam.
new.q: Papi Ours tourtons, 16 rue Pérolière, Gap

new.title: Order Marthe's gratin dauphinois at the Auberge des Montauds
new.desc: This inn at Bois Barbu above Villard-de-Lans is known for a gratin dauphinois served by the dining-room fireplace. It is also a small hotel with 11 rooms.
new.tip: Hours were undated in listings, so book and confirm before the climb up from Villard.
new.q: Auberge des Montauds, Bois Barbu, Villard-de-Lans

new.title: Taste Chartreuse chocolates at Bonnat in Voiron
new.desc: Bonnat's shop at 8 cours Senozan has held the exclusive right since 1936 to make sweets containing liqueur de Chartreuse. Regional specialities include the Chardon bleu and the Pavé de Voiron.
new.tip: Ask for the Chartreuse chocolates and the gâteau le Sphinx.
new.q: Bonnat Chocolatier, 8 cours Senozan, Voiron

new.title: Buy Bleu du Queyras at the Fromagerie de Château-Queyras
new.desc: This cooperative of ten local dairy producers sells Bleu du Queyras, Viso and Estoilie raclette, and its workshop and cellar can be visited. The Bleu du Queyras was being certified as an AOP.
new.tip: Combine it with Fort Queyras, which stands just above the village.
new.q: Fromagerie de Château-Queyras, Château-Ville-Vieille

new.title: Share the single family menu at Chez Pascal above Embrun
new.desc: Perched in the hamlet of Caléyères above Embrun, this restaurant serves one menu for everyone, with farm products and no wine list.
new.tip: Reservation is advised; there is no carte, so mention allergies when booking.
new.q: Restaurant Chez Pascal, Caléyères, Embrun

new.title: Eat trout and a hiker's board at Le Rustique in the Cité Vauban
new.desc: Le Rustique at 36 rue du Pont d'Asfeld focuses on traditional local cooking, with trout dishes and a hiker's board.
new.tip: It sits in the old town, near the Pont d'Asfeld.
new.q: Le Rustique, 36 rue du Pont d'Asfeld, Briançon

new.title: Taste Hermitage wines at the Caveau M. Chapoutier in Tain
new.desc: The Maison Chapoutier cellar shop at 18 avenue du Dr Paul Durand sells and pours the house's Rhône wines, and the shop is open to visitors without booking. The house also runs an École M. Chapoutier for tastings and cooking classes.
new.tip: Ask for an Hermitage rouge or blanc; confirm tasting hours by phone, 04 75 08 92 61.
new.q: Caveau M. Chapoutier, 18 avenue du Docteur Paul Durand, Tain-l'Hermitage

new.title: Grab bread and pastries at La Tartine Maison Ougier in Valence
new.desc: This bakery at 206 avenue Victor Hugo near Maison Pic was reported to have won the 2023 Rhône-Alpes best bakery trophy. Reviews praise its breads, viennoiseries, macarons and sandwiches.
new.tip: Open from about 6:30 to 19:00 and closed on Sundays.
new.q: La Tartine Maison Ougier, 206 avenue Victor Hugo, Valence

new.title: Browse the Thursday market of Nyons
new.desc: The weekly Thursday market is the one Nyons is known for across the region, running in the morning around the old arcades. A separate Marché provençal runs on Sunday mornings from mid-May to mid-September.
new.tip: The Thursday market runs about 8:00 to 13:00; go early in July and August.
new.q: Place des Arcades, Nyons

new.title: Drive or cycle up to the Col de Rousset tunnel
new.desc: The Col de Rousset links Die with Vassieux on the Vercors plateau through a tunnel about 800 m long, bored in 1979 at 1,254 m. It marks the climate boundary between the northern and southern Alps, and the true summit at 1,367 m can be reached on foot.
new.tip: Bring a light for the tunnel if cycling; snow may close the road in winter.
new.q: Col de Rousset, Die

new.title: Cycle the 21 hairpins up to Alpe d'Huez
new.desc: The climb from Le Bourg-d'Oisans runs 12 to 13.8 km at about 8 percent with 21 numbered hairpins, each named after a stage winner. It first appeared in the Tour de France in 1952 and has been used often since 1976.
new.tip: The signs count down from 21 at the bottom; start early in July to avoid the heat.
new.q: Départ montée de l'Alpe d'Huez, Le Bourg-d'Oisans

new.title: Hike from the Pré de Madame Carle to the Refuge du Glacier Blanc
new.desc: From the car park at 1,874 m in the Écrins National Park, the trail climbs about 4.5 km and 690 m to the refuge at 2,542 m, with views of the Glacier Blanc. The round trip takes about 4h30 to 4h45.
new.tip: Parking is paid and a shuttle from Vallouise runs in summer; start early.
new.q: Pré de Madame Carle, Pelvoux

new.title: Swim at the Charavines beach on Lac de Paladru
new.desc: Lac de Paladru has four municipal beaches, of which Charavines is the free one, supervised on Wednesdays, Saturdays and Sundays in July and August. Water temperature can reach 25 degrees in summer, and swimming is allowed only at supervised beaches.
new.tip: Dogs are not allowed on the lake beaches; Le Pin and Paladru beaches charge entry.
new.q: Plage de Charavines, Lac de Paladru, Charavines

new.title: Go caving to the underground river of the Grotte de Gournier
new.desc: The Gournier cave near Choranche has an entrance lake crossed by inflatable boat and an underground river often called among the most beautiful in the Alps. Guided descents take roughly 5 to 7 hours underground.
new.tip: Book with Immensité Nature; the trip starts at 9:00 at the Choranche caves car park.
new.q: Grotte de Gournier, Choranche

new.title: Paddle or sail on Lac de Serre-Ponçon from Chorges
new.desc: The Baie Saint-Michel beach in Chorges has nautical rentals, and bases such as the BNPA at Chorges and the Club Nautique Alpin at Savines-le-Lac rent kayaks, dinghies and paddle boards. The lake lies beneath the little Saint-Michel chapel island.
new.tip: Stand-up paddle rental was quoted at about 17 EUR per hour; confirm at the base.
new.q: Plage de la Baie Saint-Michel, Chorges

new.title: Go rafting down the Guil and Durance from Eygliers
new.desc: A family-oriented descent starts at the Pont du Simoust in Eygliers, runs class II rapids and passes beneath the Mont-Dauphin fortress on the way to Embrun. A tasting of local products is included in one offer.
new.tip: Prices start around 33 to 60 EUR depending on the length; check the operator's start point.
new.q: Pont du Simoust, Eygliers

new.title: Explore the Grands Goulets gorge in the Vercors
new.desc: The Grands Goulets road, a balcony route cut into the cliffs between 1844 and 1851 to link Pont-en-Royans and the plateau at Échevis, is now closed to traffic. A 1,710 m tunnel opened in 2008 and the gorge is explored on foot from Échevis.
new.tip: Hikers reach the area via the D518 from Pont-en-Royans or through the tunnel from Les Baraques.
new.q: Grands Goulets, Échevis

new.title: Hear the Festival Berlioz in La Côte-Saint-André
new.desc: The Festival Berlioz is held every August in La Côte-Saint-André, the composer's birthplace, and in about fifteen heritage sites of Isère including the medieval Halle and the Château Louis XI courtyard. The 33rd edition ran from 19 to 30 August 2026.
new.tip: Buy tickets online or at 38 place de la Halle; the festival runs for about twelve days in late August.
new.q: Halle de La Côte-Saint-André, place de la Halle, La Côte-Saint-André

new.title: Catch a concert at Jazz à Vienne in the Roman theatre
new.desc: Jazz à Vienne has been held at the Théâtre Antique since 1981, with ticketed concerts for about 7,500 spectators and free stages such as the Jardins de Cybèle. The 45th edition ran from 25 June to 11 July 2026.
new.tip: Tickets ranged from about 6 to 65 EUR; the next edition is expected in summer 2027.
new.q: Théâtre Antique de Vienne, Jazz à Vienne, Vienne

new.title: Join the Festival de la Correspondance in Grignan
new.desc: Held each early July since 1996, the festival offers readings, workshops and a book market at the château and in the village. The 30th edition (6 to 11 July 2026) marked 400 years since Madame de Sévigné's birth.
new.tip: The programme is normally published in June; the 2027 dates listed are 5 to 10 July.
new.q: Château de Grignan, Festival de la Correspondance, Grignan

new.title: Cycle the ViaRhôna from Tain-l'Hermitage to Valence
new.desc: The Tain to Valence stretch of ViaRhôna (EuroVelo 17) is mostly flat, with gradients that never exceed 3 percent, and includes a stabilised greenway from Tain to the La Roche-de-Glun bridge. Bike boxes in Valence let you leave a bike while sightseeing.
new.tip: Loop n°9 from Tain is 56 km and mixes vineyard roads with ViaRhôna sections.
new.q: ViaRhôna, quai du Rhône, Tain-l'Hermitage

new.title: Hike the Hauts-Plateaux du Vercors nature reserve
new.desc: Created in 1985, this 17,000 hectare reserve is the largest nature reserve in mainland France, rising from 1,050 m to 2,341 m at the Grand Veymont. Outings from Vassieux-en-Vercors include a 500 m climb around the Col de la Chau and Col de la Mure.
new.tip: Dogs are not allowed, even on a leash; many routes are unmarked so carry a map or GPS.
new.q: Vassieux-en-Vercors, Réserve naturelle des Hauts-Plateaux du Vercors

new.title: Walk to the Lac Miroir in the Queyras
new.desc: The walk to the Lac Miroir is about 4.5 km round trip in 1 to 1.5 hours and is ranked among the hiking gems of the Queyras park. Keen hikers can go on to Lac Sainte-Anne at 2,415 m, at the foot of Font Sancte (3,385 m).
new.tip: Both lakes are usually reached from Ceillac; check the current topo for the trailhead.
new.q: Lac Miroir, Ceillac

new.title: Browse the Saturday market of Vienne
new.desc: The Grand marché du samedi gathers more than 300 traders around Place de Miremont and Cours Romestang, from 6 am to 1 pm. It is free to browse.
new.tip: Vienne also has Friday and Wednesday markets at Place de Miremont.
new.q: Place de Miremont, Vienne

new.title: Hike the Grand Som in the Chartreuse from the Col du Cucheron
new.desc: The Grand Som (2,026 m) can be climbed from several routes, with the Col du Cucheron described as the simplest and shortest access, with free parking. Other routes from Saint-Pierre-d'Entremont gain about 1,000 to 1,100 m.
new.tip: Route choice depends on conditions, so check a current topo.
new.q: Col du Cucheron, Saint-Pierre-de-Chartreuse

new.title: Hike the Trois Becs above the Forêt de Saoû
new.desc: The Saoû forest is a perched syncline, among the highest in Europe, and has been owned by the Drôme department since 2003. The Trois Becs, Le Veyou (1,589 m), Le Signal and Roche Courbe, form its high point.
new.tip: The loop from the Col de la Chaudière is about 10 km with 1,100 m of ascent and takes about 6 hours.
new.q: Les Trois Becs, Forêt de Saoû, Saoû

new.title: Drive or cycle the cliff road of Combe Laval
new.desc: The road runs from Saint-Jean-en-Royans to the Col de la Machine, climbing from about 254 m to over 1,000 m, with a 6 km balcony section cut into the cliffs through tunnels. It was built in the late 19th century to haul timber.
new.tip: A vertical wall on one side and a sheer drop on the other; popular with cyclists.
new.q: Route de Combe Laval, Saint-Jean-en-Royans

new.title: Climb the Croix de Toulouse via ferrata above Briançon
new.desc: The route on the cliff of the Croix de Toulouse above Briançon is described as not difficult but long, suitable for beginners. The approach from the Champ de Mars car park takes about 30 to 40 minutes and the descent passes the Fort des Salettes.
new.tip: The season runs roughly April to the first snows; the descent path is busy with walkers in summer.
new.q: Via ferrata de la Croix de Toulouse, Champ de Mars, Briançon

new.title: Walk the Jardin du Lautaret alpine garden at 2,100 m
new.desc: This high-altitude botanical garden at the Col du Lautaret holds more than 2,000 plant species from mountains worldwide and is also a CNRS and Université Grenoble Alpes research station. Guided tours run daily at 10:30, 14:30 and 16:00.
new.tip: Open from early June to late August or early September; a ticket gives a discount on the Meije cable cars.
new.q: Jardin du Lautaret, Col du Lautaret, Villar-d'Arêne
